The rows from top to bottom contain 1, 2, 3, and 4 upward-pointing unit triangles, for a total of 10. No two of these triangles share a toothpick, so breaking all of them requires at least 10 removals.

This bound is attainable: remove all 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 horizontal toothpicks. Every triangle, regardless of size or orientation, must use all three edge directions and hence must have a horizontal side. Thus none remain.
Final answer: 10
